Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: This first round registers direct, falsifiable comparisons between molecular or technical exposures and each dependency score. For driver/gene-state hypotheses, the primary expectation is that cells carrying an activating alteration or loss in a related pathway will show a more negative dependency score (stronger dependency) in the matched or biologically connected outcome; these are registered with direction -1. For TP53 loss and MDM2 dependency, the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive because TP53 wild-type cells are often more MDM2 dependent, while TP53-loss cells may be less dependent. A technical crispr_library_avana comparison is included for a broadly essential process (POLR2A) to detect whether library-associated screen artifacts could confound later biological claims. Additional proposals cover less direct but plausible pathway links: MYC amplification with USP7/DHX9/KIF18A, EGFR amplification with TMED10, KRAS mutation with RIT1, and TP53 loss with RPL11. All proposals are initially unresolved and will be judged by effect size relative to the clinical-significance threshold, uncertainty intervals, and whether the direction matches the biological prediction. Independent validation will be reserved for findings with credible magnitude and direction.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: Estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Therefore, for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference below the comparator, i.e. stronger dependency; a negative signed estimate corresponds to the opposite raw direction. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds directly to a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator difference. The strongest new evidence supports three dataset-specific associations. H6 has signed estimate 0.784 with 95% interval 0.765 to 0.803, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly lower/more negative SMARCA2 dependency scores. H7 has signed estimate 0.790 with interval 0.760 to 0.819, meaning MSI-high cells have markedly lower WRN dependency scores. H11 has signed estimate 0.267 with interval 0.215 to 0.319, meaning PTEN-loss cells have lower STAT3 dependency scores. These effects are very large relative to the outcome scales and well beyond the 10% clinical-significance scale, so I accept H6, H7, and H11 within this dataset, while reserving mechanistic and generalizability claims. H5 is opposite to the registered direction: with direction -1, the signed estimate is -0.796, implying a raw positive difference of about +0.796. Thus KEAP1-loss cells have higher/less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores, so the original H5 claim is rejected and a reversed parent-linked claim is proposed. H3 is the most informative borderline claim: EGFR amplification is associated with a signed difference of about 0.025, near the 10% relative scale, but the interval barely includes zero. I leave H3 unresolved and request independent validation because validation is most useful for a clinically borderline claim. Most other direct comparisons are either tiny and opposite, or imprecise with intervals that cross zero. H2 and H10 are rejected because their intervals do not support a clinically meaningful effect in the expected direction. H1, H4, H8, and H9 are deferred: their point estimates are not compelling, but the intervals are broad enough that I do not want to overclaim rejection at this stage. H12 is a technical library control for a broadly essential process; it is imprecise and not followed further, though the large accepted biological effects remain subject to specificity checks. To assess possible global confounding behind H6, H7, H11, and reversed H5, I registered POLR2A negative-control comparisons for SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, and KEAP1 loss. POLR2A has relatively small variance and is expected to be broadly essential; large differences in POLR2A by these exposures would raise concern that the observed associations reflect broader cell-state or technical confounding rather than gene-specific dependency relationships.

record.narrative:
The new validation evidence for H3 changes the assessment of the EGFR claim. H3 was registered with direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference below the comparator, meaning stronger EGFR dependency in EGFR-amplified cells. The discovery estimate for H3 was signed +0.025, which was near a roughly 10% relative effect scale but had a 95% interval that barely included zero. The independent validation estimate is signed only +0.006, with interval -0.034 to +0.045. Interpreted on the raw scale, validation therefore shows an EGFR-amplified minus non-amplified difference of about -0.006 EGFR dependency units, roughly 2% relative to the EGFR dependency mean, with uncertainty including null and clinically meaningful differences in both directions. The validation point estimate is far below the clinical-significance threshold and does not corroborate the borderline discovery result. Therefore the combined evidence does not support a reliable clinically meaningful association between EGFR amplification and stronger EGFR dependency in this dataset; H3 is rejected and closed.

I also reassess the reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 claim H17 using the same direct discovery evidence that caused the original H5 direction to be rejected. H17 is registered with direction +1, and its evidence is signed +0.796 with a very tight interval +0.776 to +0.816. On the raw scale, this means KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact cells, by a magnitude far above a 10% relative effect scale. This association is very large and precisely estimated within this dataset, so I accept H17 as a dataset-specific association while explicitly reserving mechanistic or generalizability claims. The original H5 claim remains rejected because the observed direction is opposite to the pre-specified stronger-dependency direction.

The previously accepted H6, H7, and H11 remain supported associations in this dataset: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency; and PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. The technical POLR2A library control was not informative, and the next priority is specificity. If SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, or KEAP1 loss also produces large differences in the broadly essential POLR2A dependency score, that would suggest global screen or cell-state confounding and should lead to reassessment of these accepted associations. The most informative next analyses are therefore the reversed KEAP1-loss claim H17 already registered, the four POLR2A specificity controls H18-H21, and the still-untested direct pathway comparisons H13-H16. If the POLR2A controls are null, the accepted associations can remain strong dataset-specific findings; if any control is large, I will downgrade the corresponding accepted association as possibly non-specific. These conclusions are not causal and do not establish generalizability beyond the supplied dataset.

Iteration 2/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: I am registering four targeted new comparisons to run alongside the eight already untested registered comparisons H13-H16 and H18-H21, so the next analysis batch can contain 12 informative tests. The accepted claims so far are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency. The four new claims are designed to test nearby biology and context effects rather than repeat existing comparisons. First, arid1a_loss versus intact is a new direct predictor for dependency_SMARCA2. ARID1A and SMARCA4 are SWI/SNF complex components, so loss of another BAF component could produce a similar synthetic-lethal-like dependency on SMARCA2; registered direction -1 expects a more negative dependency score in arid1a-loss cells. Second, pik3ca_mutation versus wild type is a direct test for dependency_STAT3. Activating PIK3CA mutations can increase PI3K/AKT/STAT3 signaling, and PTEN loss already showed a positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency, so I anticipate a more negative STAT3 dependency score in PIK3CA-mutant cells; direction -1. Third, tp53_loss versus intact is a direct test for dependency_USP7. USP7 participates in MDM2-p53 regulation, and cells with TP53 loss are plausibly less dependent on USP7 through that axis, which would appear as a higher/less-negative dependency score in TP53-loss cells; direction +1. Fourth, EGFR dependency in KRAS wild-type versus KRAS mutant cells tests molecular context after EGFR amplification alone failed validation. If KRAS mutant cells bypass EGFR, they may be less EGFR-dependent, producing a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast for KRAS wild type and thus a positive signed estimate under direction -1. Alternative outcomes are null or opposite associations, which would argue against these mechanistic predictions and would be treated as evidence that the associations are not general across measured molecular contexts in this dataset. These claims are dataset-specific associations only; causality, therapeutic implication, and generalizability remain outside the immediate evidence.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new batch mostly rejects the smaller pathway hypotheses and produces one very strong new association. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates mean weaker/higher dependency. H13-KRAS mutation with RIT1, H14-TP53 loss with RPL11, H15-MYC amplification with KIF18A, H16-EGFR amplification with TMED10, H22-ARID1A loss with SMARCA2, H23-PIK3CA mutation with STAT3, and H25-KRAS wild-type versus KRAS-mutant EGFR dependency all have point estimates near zero and intervals dominated by null; their upper bounds are at or below the roughly 10% clinical threshold. I reject these as unsupported dataset-specific associations and close them. H22 and H23 are important boundaries: the strong SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association does not extend to ARID1A loss, and the strong PTEN-loss/STAT3 association does not extend to PIK3CA mutation in this dataset. The POLR2A specificity controls H18-H21 are not informative positives: point estimates are tiny (about 0.4%-3% relative to POLR2A mean) and none approaches the enormous scale of accepted associations, although some intervals extend into the 10% region. This reduces, but does not eliminate, concern about global screen or cell-state confounding, so accepted H6, H7, H11, and H17 remain active dataset-specific associations. The major new result is H24: TP53 loss versus intact for dependency_USP7 has signed estimate +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467. Because H24 direction is +1, this is a raw positive difference: TP53-loss cells have markedly higher/less-negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, than TP53-intact cells. This is far above the 10% threshold and tightly bounded away from zero, so I accept H24 within this dataset. This is surprising because H8 TP53 loss with MDM2 was null, so I request independent validation of H24 before interpreting the mechanism. I also registered a POLR2A TP53-loss specificity control and a TP53-loss-by-KRAS-mutation interaction for USP7 to test whether H24 is non-specific or context-dependent. These conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H24 strongly supports the TP53-loss/USP7 association. H24 has direction +1, so the reported signed estimates are raw exposed-minus-comparator differences on the dependency_USP7 scale. Discovery was +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467. Validation was +0.437 with independent interval +0.336 to +0.537. Because this is a direction +1 claim, a positive value means TP53-loss cells have higher, less-negative USP7 dependency scores than TP53-intact cells, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. The magnitude is far larger than a roughly 10% relative effect threshold and remains bounded away from zero even under the stringent validation interval, so I accept H24 as a robust dataset-specific association. This does not establish causality or generalizability beyond the supplied dataset; it establishes that the association is stable within the supplied experimental system and validation split. I keep H24 active because context and specificity analyses remain useful. The prior POLR2A specificity controls for SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, and KEAP1 loss had very small point estimates relative to the large accepted associations, reducing concern about generic screen or cell-state confounding, but the TP53-loss POLR2A control H26 is still pending. The newly registered interactions ask whether accepted associations are stable across measured contexts: SMARCA4-loss effect by ARID1A loss for SMARCA2, PTEN-loss effect by PIK3CA mutation for STAT3, MSI-high effect by lineage subtype for WRN, and KEAP1-loss effect by STK11 loss for NFE2L2. The new USP7 cross-specificity proposals test whether SMARCA4 loss or PTEN loss also produce TP53-like USP7 effects. If those controls are large, I would downgrade the apparent specificity of the corresponding accepted associations; if they are near null, the accepted associations become more credible as dataset-specific, predictor-specific patterns. The next most informative analyses are therefore H26 and H27 plus these context/specificity proposals.

Activating PIK3CA mutations can increase PI3K/AKT/STAT3 signaling, and PTEN loss already showed a positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency, so I anticipate a more negative STAT3 dependency score in PIK3CA-mutant cells; direction -1. Third, tp53_loss versus intact is a direct test for dependency_USP7. USP7 participates in MDM2-p53 regulation, and cells with TP53 loss are plausibly less dependent on USP7 through that axis, which would appear as a higher/less-negative dependency score in TP53-loss cells; direction +1. Fourth, EGFR dependency in KRAS wild-type versus KRAS mutant cells tests molecular context after EGFR amplification alone failed validation. If KRAS mutant cells bypass EGFR, they may be less EGFR-dependent, producing a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast for KRAS wild type and thus a positive signed estimate under direction -1. H22 and H23 are important boundaries: the strong SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association does not extend to ARID1A loss, and the strong PTEN-loss/STAT3 association does not extend to PIK3CA mutation in this dataset. The major new result is H24: TP53 loss versus intact for dependency_USP7 has signed estimate +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467. Because H24 direction is +1, this is a raw positive difference: TP53-loss cells have markedly higher/less-negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, than TP53-intact cells. This is far above the 10% threshold and tightly bounded away from zero, so I accept H24 within this dataset. This is surprising because H8 TP53 loss with MDM2 was null, so I request independent validation of H24 before interpreting the mechanism. This batch is the maximum informative set because it combines the still-pending TP53-loss POLR2A specificity control (H26), key context-interaction tests for accepted associations (H27-H31), direct USP7 cross-specificity checks for SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss (H32-H33), WRN/SMARCA2 cross-specificity checks (H34-H35), and the two new reciprocal specificity checks for NFE2L2/SMARCA4 loss and WRN/KEAP1 loss (H36-H37). If POLR2A and cross-specificity controls are near null, the accepted associations remain credible as dataset-specific, predictor-specific patterns. These remain association analyses in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizability claims.

Iteration 3/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new batch is dominated by well-behaved null and near-null control analyses, and it strengthens the internal credibility of the already accepted dataset-specific associations rather than adding new large effects. All estimates are already signed to the claim direction. H26 is the TP53-loss specificity control for POLR2A: signed estimate -0.014, 95% CI -0.034 to +0.006, n=406/1594. The point is about 5% of the POLR2A mean magnitude and is statistically compatible with zero; I reject it as an unsupported meaningful TP53-loss/POLR2A association and close it. This supports, though it does not prove, that the accepted TP53-loss/USP7 effect is not simply a global screen or essentiality shift. H27-H31 test context dependence. H27 USP7-by-KRAS interaction (+0.018, CI -0.152 to +0.188), H28 SMARCA2-by-ARID1A-loss interaction (+0.037, CI -0.015 to +0.089), H29 STAT3-by-PIK3CA interaction (+0.001, CI -0.150 to +0.152), H30 WRN-by-adenocarcinoma interaction (-0.021, CI -0.085 to +0.042), and H31 NFE2L2-by-STK11-loss interaction (-0.026, CI -0.079 to +0.026) all have point estimates below the roughly 10% clinical-scale criterion and include zero. I reject each as unsupported evidence for meaningful modification in this dataset, while noting that some subgroup intervals are wide and therefore do not establish precise absence of heterogeneity. H32-H37 are predictor-specificity controls. SMARCA4 loss or PTEN loss do not affect USP7 dependency (H32: -0.002; H33: -0.005). SMARCA4 loss does not affect WRN dependency (H34: +0.003), PTEN loss does not meaningfully affect SMARCA2 dependency (H35: +0.018, about 4% of the SMARCA2 mean), SMARCA4 loss does not affect NFE2L2 dependency (H36: -0.012), and KEAP1 loss does not affect WRN dependency (H37: +0.007). These controls are near null on the scale of the accepted effects, so they reduce concern that accepted associations reflect broad cell-state or technical confounding and increase the apparent predictor specificity of accepted H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24 within this dataset. I am requesting independent validation of H7 (MSI-high and dependency_WRN) because it is a large accepted effect in a relatively small MSI-high subgroup, and independent stability would make it a more reliable dataset-specific claim. No new causal or external-generalizability claim is made.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed value supports the claimed direction. H38-H49 were mostly technical-context or predictor-specificity controls. H38 (SMARCA2/SMARCA4 by Avana, signed -0.0198, 95% CI -0.0762 to +0.0365), H39 (NFE2L2/KEAP1 by Avana, +0.0022, -0.0506 to +0.0550), and H41 (USP7/TP53 by Avana, +0.0837, -0.1632 to +0.3306) do not provide reliable evidence for meaningful modification of the accepted SMARCA4, KEAP1, or TP53 main effects. The H41 point is not negligible, but the interval is extremely wide and includes zero; the non-Avana TP53-loss cell is small. I reject these as unsupported context effects. H43-H49 are new predictors or cross-specificity checks; all point estimates are small or statistically compatible with zero: BRCA2 loss on WRN, STK11 loss on NFE2L2, MSI-high on DHX9, SMARCA4 loss on STAT3, KEAP1 loss on SMARCA2, TP53 loss on NFE2L2, and PTEN loss on WRN. I reject these as unsupported associations, while noting that confidence intervals are not formal equivalence bounds. The two exceptions are H40 and H42. H40 (PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 modified by Avana library) has signed estimate +0.1958, 95% CI +0.0333 to +0.3584; the point is about 70% of the validated PTEN-loss main effect on STAT3, but the non-Avana PTEN-loss cell has only 27 exposed samples, so I keep it unresolved and active rather than accepting an unadjusted, possibly unstable context claim. H42 (MSI-high effect on WRN modified by adherent culture) has signed estimate +0.1046, 95% CI +0.0370 to +0.1722. The lower bound is just above the approximate 10% outcome-mean scale for dependency_WRN, but the comparison involves a small non-adherent MSI-high cell and multiple unadjusted tests. I keep H42 unresolved and active and request independent validation of H42; validation will decide whether the culture-dependent difference is stable enough to refine the robust H7 claim. The original main effects H7 and H11 remain accepted as overall dataset-specific associations, but I keep their investigations active because these context interactions may be important refinements.

Iteration 4/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For H24 (TP53 loss versus intact, direction +1, dependency_USP7), discovery was +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467) and independent validation was +0.437 (independent interval +0.336 to +0.537). This is a very large effect on the dependency_USP7 scale and is bounded away from zero after independent validation. I therefore accept H24 as a robust dataset-specific association and close it: TP53 loss is associated with weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency in this dataset. This is not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H42 (adherent-culture modification of the MSI-high/WRN effect, direction -1), discovery gave +0.105 (95% CI +0.037 to +0.172), but independent validation gave -0.011 (independent interval -0.121 to +0.099). The validation point is essentially null and opposite in sign, and the independent interval does not support a stable positive adherent-culture interaction. I reject H42 as a supported context-specific refinement, while noting that its validation interval is not an equivalence proof against every possible small or opposite interaction. This rejection does not undermine the overall MSI-high/WRN claim: H7 remains robustly accepted with discovery +0.790 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.819) and independent validation +0.822 (independent interval +0.776 to +0.868). Given the validated main effect and the failed culture interaction, I close H7. I also close the main H11 association because PTEN-loss/STAT3 was validated (+0.309, independent interval +0.232 to +0.386). However, H40 remains active because its discovery library interaction is still potentially important; the registered simple-effect analyses in Avana and non-Avana library contexts (H51 and H52) are the appropriate next refinement. Current robust dataset-specific associations are H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24, with H6 and H17 now the highest-priority unvalidated accepted effects. The next best analyses are H50-H52: check whether WRN/MSI-high remains strong within adherent culture, and decompose the PTEN-loss/STAT3 library-context signal. After those, validation should target H6 first, then H17. These conclusions describe associations in the supplied data, not causality or generalizable biology.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.
