First, three predictor-specific biological hypotheses test additional measured binary predictors: MYC amplification may strengthen dependency_POLR2A because MYC-amplified cells can be transcription-addicted; RB1 loss may strengthen dependency_WRN through replication-stress biology; NF1 loss may alter dependency_STAT3 through RAS/MAPK and inflammatory-signal rewiring. A large positive signed interaction would support a subtype-specific refinement; a small or zero interaction would support treating the parent effects as broader within this dataset. The active H50-H52 remain important for decomposing WRN/MSI-high adherent-cell behavior and PTEN-loss/STAT3 library context. Validation priority remains H6 then H17 after the next discovery results arrive.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claim and negative values oppose it. Using an approximate absolute 10% outcome-mean scale for clinical significance, H50 (MSI-high effect on dependency_WRN within adherent culture) has a very large signed estimate of +0.813 with 95% CI +0.780 to +0.846, far above the relevant WRN threshold and with adequate cells; I accept it as a dataset-specific refinement supporting the robust overall MSI-high/WRN association. H51 (PTEN-loss effect on dependency_STAT3 within Avana library) has estimate +0.288, CI +0.232 to +0.343, also robustly clinically meaningful and consistent with the validated main PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect; I accept and close it. H52 (PTEN-loss/STAT3 within non-Avana library) has point +0.092, but the interval is wide (-0.062 to +0.246) and the exposed non-Avana cell has only 27 samples; this is too unstable to accept or reject, so I defer it. The remaining new comparisons provide no reliable evidence for clinically meaningful claimed associations. H53 has point +0.0039 and upper bound +0.0251, essentially below the POLR2A clinical scale. H54 has point +0.0154 and interval -0.0216 to +0.0525; it does not support the claimed RB1-loss/WRN effect, although the interval is not an equivalence bound. H55 has a signed estimate opposite to the claimed direction and upper bound below the STAT3 clinical threshold. H56, H57, and H58 are tiny or opposite-signed and their upper bounds do not establish 10% clinical effects. H59-H61 test lineage-subtype modification of the large accepted associations; all point estimates are small or opposite in sign and the intervals do not support meaningful adenocarcinoma-versus-non-adenocarcinoma modification of H6, H17, or H11. Given multiple unadjusted discovery tests, I reject these unsupported associations while noting that confidence intervals are not formal equivalence proof for every possible small or opposite effect. Given the currently unvalidated status and large discovery effect size of H6 (SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency), I request independent validation of H6 now. Pending that validation, H17 remains the next highest-priority accepted unvalidated association.

Iteration 5/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive estimates support the claimed direction and negative estimates oppose it. For H6 (SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, registered direction -1), discovery was +0.784 (95% CI +0.765 to +0.803), and independent validation was +0.780 with a much wider independent interval +0.749 to +0.810. The validation effect is essentially concordant with discovery, has adequate cells, and is far above any plausible clinically significant scale for dependency_SMARCA2. I therefore accept H6 as a robust dataset-specific association: SMARCA4-loss cell lines show stronger, more negative dependency on SMARCA2 in this dataset. This is an association, not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H7 (MSI-high versus dependency_WRN, direction -1), discovery +0.790 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.819) was independently validated at +0.822 (independent interval +0.776 to +0.868), remaining large and clearly above the clinical-significance threshold. I accept and close H7 as a robust dataset-specific MSI-high/WRN association, despite the earlier failure of the adherent-culture interaction refinement H42. For H11 (PTEN loss versus dependency_STAT3, direction -1), discovery +0.267 (95% CI +0.215 to +0.319) was independently validated at +0.309 (independent interval +0.232 to +0.386). This effect is also clearly above the relevant clinical threshold and stable under validation; I accept and close H11. H24 (TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7) was previously accepted and independently validated and remains a robust dataset-specific association with weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines. H17 (KEAP1 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2, direction +1) remains accepted on discovery evidence alone, with a very large signed discovery estimate +0.796, but it has not yet received independent validation; it is now the highest-priority unvalidated accepted effect. Overall supported dataset-specific findings are therefore H6, H7, H11, H24, and provisionally H17, with H50 and H51 accepted as strong context simple-effect refinements of H7 and H11, respectively. Negative or unsupported findings include failed culture/library/lineage/predictor interactions for several accepted effects, unsupported research-marker associations, and rejected small predictor effects including MYC/POLR2A, RB1/WRN, NF1/STAT3, and numerous cross-specificity checks; these should not be read as formal equivalence proofs, especially for intervals that can still include small effects. Remaining unresolved uncertainty is mainly limited-power context estimates, especially H40/H52 for non-Avana PTEN-loss/STAT3 context, and a few unresolved main associations such as KRAS mutation/dependency_KRAS, ERBB2 amplification/dependency_ERBB2, TP53 loss/dependency_MDM2, and MYC amplification/dependency_USP7. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H17 using the original claim. If H17 validates, it should be closed as a robust dataset-specific KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency association; if it fails, the accepted set must be reassessed. After H17, validation or further targeted exploration should focus on the remaining borderline unresolved main associations rather than on interactions that already failed validation or are too small in discovery.

Second, I refine unresolved MYC-related claims: MYC amplification versus dependency_MDM2 restricted to TP53-wild-type cell lines, because MYC-induced p53-pathway dependency should be strongest when p53 is intact; and MYC amplification versus dependency_USP7 restricted to high MYC RNA expression, testing whether functional MYC expression reveals an effect missed by binary amplification. Third, I refine borderline receptor-pathway claims: KRAS mutation versus dependency_KRAS within STK11-wild-type cell lines, because KRAS-mutant dependency may be strongest in non-LKB1-loss KRAS biology; and ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 within EGFR-non-amplified cell lines, because receptor-pathway specificity may be diluted when EGFR is co-amplified. record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claim and negative values oppose it. H17 (KEAP1 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2, direction +1) now has independent validation: discovery +0.796 with 95% CI +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation +0.792 with an independent interval +0.762 to +0.822. The two estimates are nearly identical, the intervals are far from zero and far above any clinically significant 10% scale for dependency_NFE2L2, and the cell counts are adequate. I therefore accept H17 and close it as a robust dataset-specific association: in this dataset, KEAP1-loss lines have a less negative/WEAKER dependency_NFE2L2 score than KEAP1-intact lines. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

few unresolved main effects that still have plausible biological contexts. I prioritize three kinds of comparisons. First, I add robustness/context refinements for the strongly accepted dataset-specific associations. These are not meant to claim causality or external generalizability; they ask whether the accepted effect is still large in biologically or technically plausible strata: MSI-high versus dependency_WRN among high Cas9 activity; KEAP1-loss versus dependency_NFE2L2 modified by TP53 loss; TP53-loss versus dependency_USP7 among MYC-amplified lines and modified by KEAP1 loss; PTEN-loss versus dependency_STAT3 and SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 among high screen quality, using screen_roc_auc >= 0.95. I expect the accepted large effects to remain signed in the accepted direction and far above the approximate 10% clinical-significance scale if they are not context-specific or technical. If intervals are wide or the interval lower bound remains near the clinical threshold, I would keep the context unresolved rather than accept. Second, I add pathway-specific refinements for receptor/MAPK dependencies. EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR within KRAS wild type, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 within KRAS wild type, and KRAS mutation versus dependency_KRAS within EGFR-nonamplified are plausible because receptor-pathway dependency may be stronger when downstream or parallel RAS biology is intact and less confounded by alternative activating lesions. These are refinements of previously rejected/deferred main associations, and they remain dataset-specific tests; prior nulls do not prove equivalence, especially with wide intervals. Third, I add p53/USP7-MYC and WRN cross-context comparisons. TP53 loss versus dependency_MDM2 among MYC-amplified lines tests whether the expected p53-loss effect on MDM2 dependency appears in a MYC-driven p53-pathway context. MYC amplification versus dependency_USP7 among TP53-loss lines tests whether MYC biology modifies the p53-loss-associated USP7 dependency. TP53 loss versus dependency_WRN among MSI-negative lines tests whether TP53 loss has an effect on WRN that is not simply a reflection of MSI co-occurrence. These are exploratory but interpretable. I reopened H1, H4, H8, and H9 as active because I registered refinements targeting them; this does not mean their main effects are accepted. record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claimed direction and negative values oppose it. For these dependency-score comparisons, I used the pre-specified approximate 10% clinically meaningful scale (about 0.1 in this standardized/score-scale setting) as the main magnitude benchmark, while also requiring that 95% intervals exclude the null and not be compatible with negligible effects after accounting for multiple discovery tests. H74, H75, H77, H78, H79, H80, H82, and H84 have very large signed point estimates with lower bounds far above 0.1 and adequate cells, so I accept them as dataset-specific context simple effects. These mainly reinforce robustness of previously validated associations under high-assay-quality or pathway strata: MSI-high remains strongly associated with more negative WRN dependency in high mutation burden, high Cas9 activity, and high screen ROC; SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with more negative SMARCA2 dependency under high screen ROC; KEAP1 loss remains strongly associated with less negative NFE2L2 dependency among high research signature C and among TP53-wild-type lines; PTEN loss remains associated with more negative STAT3 dependency under high screen ROC. H84 additionally supports that TP53 loss is associated with less negative USP7 dependency within MYC-amplified lines, although the exposed cell is smaller (n=60), so this remains a context-specific dataset association rather than evidence of causal effect modification. I reject H81, H83, H85, and H88. H81 and H83 are interactions with signed estimates near zero and intervals that cross zero and remain within a small range, so they do not support effect modification by TP53 loss or KRAS mutation. H85 is signed negative, with an interval crossing zero and an upper bound below 0.1, so there is no support for stronger MYC-amplification-associated USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines. H88 is near zero and imprecise, so TP53 loss within MYC-amplified lines does not show clinically meaningful MDM2 dependency difference. H74, H75, H77, H78, H79, H80, and H82 are not separately validated, but they are stratum estimates of already large validated main effects and are too consistent to justify validation on their own; I therefore close them as accepted dataset-specific context effects. The most useful validation target remains H51, PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency within Avana-library lines, because H51 is an accepted but unvalidated context effect and the related library-context interaction H40 is unresolved. I request independent validation of H51. These conclusions remain limited to associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability. I propose a direct interaction test for TP53 loss on USP7 dependency by MYC-amplification status, motivated by the large H84 simple effect, to assess whether MYC context actually modifies the TP53 loss association.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

I register follow-up comparisons that either resolve currently active biology or test meaningful context boundaries around the strongest accepted dataset associations. For these continuous dependency scores, I will use the approximate absolute 0.1 score difference scale as a rough meaningful benchmark, consistent with prior appraisals, while requiring adequate cells and interval precision.  The USP7/TP53 question is the highest-priority follow-up. H84 suggested that TP53 loss is associated with much weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency within MYC-amplified lines, while broad H24 is already accepted and H90 tests the non-MYC-amplified simple effect. I therefore add TP53-loss/USP7 tests stratified by MYC expression rather than amplification alone: a high-MYC-expression simple effect, a low-MYC-expression simple effect, and a direct interaction. If the low-expression effect remains large, the TP53-loss association is likely broad; if it is much weaker than the high-expression/MYC-amplified effect, this supports MYC-context dependence rather than a general USP7 association. These are associations and not causal effect-modification claims.  For KEAP1/NFE2L2, H80 established the accepted association within TP53-wildtype lines and H81 failed to support interaction by TP53 loss, but a simple effect within TP53-loss lines is still useful to determine whether the effect is broadly present across TP53 status. I also test whether high hypoxia amplifies the weaker NFE2L2 dependency associated with KEAP1 loss, since NFE2L2 governs oxidative-stress biology and hypoxic microenvironments could interact with NRF2 pathway dependency.  For MSI-high/WRN, I test two complementary context boundaries. First, whether high interferon-gamma signature strengthens the WRN dependency effect, because MSI-high tumors are often immunogenic and this could identify a biologically meaningful subgroup. Second, whether the association persists in lower screen-quality/low screen ROC lines; persistence would support technical robustness, while attenuation would warrant caution about assay-quality dependence.  For weaker or active pathway questions, I test TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss lines to probe the p53-MDM2/CDKN2A axis, KRAS mutation on dependency_KRAS within low mutation burden to test whether oncogene specificity is more visible in cleaner genomic backgrounds, and ERBB2 amplification on dependency_ERBB2 in a driver-exclusion context (EGFR non-amplified, KRAS wild-type, and relatively low AXL) to see whether ERBB2 dependency emerges when alternative RTK/RAS drivers are less prominent. All proposals remain dataset-specific hypothesis tests; acceptance will require signed effects consistent with the claimed direction and intervals that support a magnitude of at least roughly the 0.1 meaningful scale.","analyze":"No assessments are due because no new discovery or validation evidence is pending. The first priority is to resolve the USP7/TP53 context question: H89 directly tests MYC-amplification modification of TP53 loss; H90 tests TP53 loss in non-MYC-amplified lines; H91 and H92 test high versus low MYC expression simple effects; and H93 tests whether MYC expression itself modifies the TP53-loss association. Together these distinguish a broad TP53-loss association with less negative USP7 dependency from a MYC-context-specific association. The second priority is to assess context boundaries for accepted pathway associations: H94 tests KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency within TP53-loss lines to complement the accepted TP53-wildtype effect; H95 tests whether hypoxia amplifies that association; H96 tests whether interferon-gamma signature modifies MSI-high/WRN dependency; and H97 tests whether MSI-high/WRN remains meaningful in lower screen-quality lines, a robustness check. The third priority is to probe weaker active pathway hypotheses: H98 tests TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss lines; H99 tests KRAS-mutant specificity in lower mutation-burden lines; and H100 tests ERBB2 amplification in a driver-exclusion context of EGFR non-amplification, KRAS wild-type status, and relatively low AXL expression. All requested estimates will be signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I will accept only effects with signed lower bounds clearly above the approximate 0.1 meaningful scale and adequate cells; near-null or imprecise estimates will remain unresolved or rejected as unsupported in this dataset, not as evidence of true absence.","appraise":"All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claimed direction and negative values oppose it. For these dependency-score comparisons, I used the pre-specified approximate 10% clinically meaningful scale (about 0.1 in this standardized/score-scale setting) as the main magnitude benchmark, while also requiring that 95% intervals exclude the null and not be compatible with negligible effects after accounting for multiple discovery tests. H74, H75, H77, H78, H79, H80, H82, and H84 have very large signed point estimates with lower bounds far above 0.1 and adequate cells, so I accept them as dataset-specific context simple effects. These mainly reinforce robustness of previously validated associations under high-assay-quality or pathway strata: MSI-high remains strongly associated with more negative WRN dependency in high mutation burden, high Cas9 activity, and high screen ROC; SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with more negative SMARCA2 dependency under high screen ROC; KEAP1 loss remains strongly associated with less negative NFE2L2 dependency among high research signature C and among TP53-wild-type lines; PTEN loss remains associated with more negative STAT3 dependency under high screen ROC. H84 additionally supports that TP53 loss is associated with less negative USP7 dependency within MYC-amplified lines, although the exposed cell is smaller (n=60), so this remains a context-specific dataset association rather than evidence of causal effect modification. I reject H81, H83, H85, and H88. H81 and H83 are interactions with signed estimates near zero and intervals that cross zero and remain within a small range, so they do not support effect modification by TP53 loss or KRAS mutation. H85 is signed negative, with an interval crossing zero and an upper bound below 0.1, so there is no support for stronger MYC-amplification-associated USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines. H88 is near zero and imprecise, so TP53 loss within MYC-amplified lines does not show clinically meaningful MDM2 dependency difference. H74, H75, H77, H78, H79, H80, and H82 are not separately validated, but they are stratum estimates of already large validated main effects and are too consistent to justify validation on their own; I therefore close them as accepted dataset-specific context effects. The most useful validation target remains H51, PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency within Avana-library lines, because H51 is an accepted but unvalidated context effect and the related library-context interaction H40 is unresolved. For these continuous dependency scores, I will use the approximate absolute 0.1 score difference scale as a rough meaningful benchmark, consistent with prior appraisals, while requiring adequate cells and interval precision.  The USP7/TP53 question is the highest-priority follow-up. H84 suggested that TP53 loss is associated with much weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency within MYC-amplified lines, while broad H24 is already accepted and H90 tests the non-MYC-amplified simple effect. I therefore add TP53-loss/USP7 tests stratified by MYC expression rather than amplification alone: a high-MYC-expression simple effect, a low-MYC-expression simple effect, and a direct interaction. If the low-expression effect remains large, the TP53-loss association is likely broad; if it is much weaker than the high-expression/MYC-amplified effect, this supports MYC-context dependence rather than a general USP7 association. These are associations and not causal effect-modification claims.  For KEAP1/NFE2L2, H80 established the accepted association within TP53-wildtype lines and H81 failed to support interaction by TP53 loss, but a simple effect within TP53-loss lines is still useful to determine whether the effect is broadly present across TP53 status. I also test whether high hypoxia amplifies the weaker NFE2L2 dependency associated with KEAP1 loss, since NFE2L2 governs oxidative-stress biology and hypoxic microenvironments could interact with NRF2 pathway dependency.  For MSI-high/WRN, I test two complementary context boundaries. First, whether high interferon-gamma signature strengthens the WRN dependency effect, because MSI-high tumors are often immunogenic and this could identify a biologically meaningful subgroup. Second, whether the association persists in lower screen-quality/low screen ROC lines; persistence would support technical robustness, while attenuation would warrant caution about assay-quality dependence.  For weaker or active pathway questions, I test TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss lines to probe the p53-MDM2/CDKN2A axis, KRAS mutation on dependency_KRAS within low mutation burden to test whether oncogene specificity is more visible in cleaner genomic backgrounds, and ERBB2 amplification on dependency_ERBB2 in a driver-exclusion context (EGFR non-amplified, KRAS wild-type, and relatively low AXL) to see whether ERBB2 dependency emerges when alternative RTK/RAS drivers are less prominent. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No evidence assessment is due. I register new follow-up comparisons that prioritize scientifically meaningful refinements of the accepted dataset associations and two new oncogene-pathway hypotheses. As before, I treat an approximate absolute dependency-score difference of 0.1 as a practical stand-in for the 10% clinical-significance scale, because relative differences are awkward when scores are near zero; acceptance will require signed effect estimates and intervals compatible with at least that magnitude and adequate cell counts. For direction -1 claims, a positive returned estimate supports the claim and means exposed-minus-comparator was more negative, i.e., stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive returned estimate supports less-negative dependency. The USP7/TP53 axis remains the most useful follow-up target because the broad H24 association is accepted but the small MYC-amplified context H84 attenuated on validation. I therefore test TP53 loss on USP7 dependency within KRAS-mutant lines, which can clarify whether the broad association remains present in an important molecular context even though the KRAS interaction test was unsupported. I also test whether high aneuploidy modifies the four strongest accepted dependencies: MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3. This asks whether genome instability amplifies or attenuates these associations, using a moderate high-aneuploidy cutoff of 0.45 chosen to preserve adequate cells. For MSI-high/WRN, I additionally test two technical/assay contexts: within screen_batch batch_a and within lower Cas9 activity, complementing the accepted high Cas9 context. Persistence in these strata would strengthen the dataset-specific MSI-high/WRN conclusion; attenuation would identify an important assay-quality boundary. Finally, I register two new oncogene hypotheses: BRAF V600E may be associated with weaker/less-negative KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type lines if BRAF mutation bypasses KRAS, and EGFR amplification may be associated with stronger/more-negative RIT1 dependency in KRAS-wild-type lines if downstream RAS-family signaling is engaged. These are hypotheses in this supplied dataset only, not causal claims.

As before, I treat an approximate absolute dependency-score difference of 0.1 as a practical stand-in for the 10% clinical-significance scale, because relative differences are awkward when scores are near zero; acceptance will require signed effect estimates and intervals compatible with at least that magnitude and adequate cell counts. For direction -1 claims, a positive returned estimate supports the claim and means exposed-minus-comparator was more negative, i.e., stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive returned estimate supports less-negative dependency. The USP7/TP53 axis remains the most useful follow-up target because the broad H24 association is accepted but the small MYC-amplified context H84 attenuated on validation. I therefore test TP53 loss on USP7 dependency within KRAS-mutant lines, which can clarify whether the broad association remains present in an important molecular context even though the KRAS interaction test was unsupported. I also test whether high aneuploidy modifies the four strongest accepted dependencies: MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3. This asks whether genome instability amplifies or attenuates these associations, using a moderate high-aneuploidy cutoff of 0.45 chosen to preserve adequate cells. For MSI-high/WRN, I additionally test two technical/assay contexts: within screen_batch batch_a and within lower Cas9 activity, complementing the accepted high Cas9 context. Persistence in these strata would strengthen the dataset-specific MSI-high/WRN conclusion; attenuation would identify an important assay-quality boundary. Finally, I register two new oncogene hypotheses: BRAF V600E may be associated with weaker/less-negative KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type lines if BRAF mutation bypasses KRAS, and EGFR amplification may be associated with stronger/more-negative RIT1 dependency in KRAS-wild-type lines if downstream RAS-family signaling is engaged. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the stated direction. I used the same practical 0.1 absolute dependency-score-difference benchmark, requiring adequate cells and an interval that excludes zero and supports at least that magnitude. H76 is near null for TP53 loss on WRN dependency in the claimed direction (R108: -0.005; 95% CI -0.034 to +0.023), so I reject it. H86 and H87 are also near-null or opposed in important driver-exclusive contexts: KRAS mutation among BRAF wild-type lines (R109: +0.014; CI -0.004 to +0.032) and ERBB2 amplification among KRAS wild-type lines (R110: -0.009; CI -0.042 to +0.024). Their upper bounds are below 0.1, so I reject both as not scientifically meaningful in this dataset. H101 shows a large TP53-loss-associated less-negative USP7 dependency within KRAS-mutant lines (R111: +0.410; 95% CI +0.260 to +0.561; cells 90/420), so I accept it and close the context check; it supports the broad validated TP53/USP7 association rather than KRAS-mutation-specific restriction. The four high-aneuploidy interaction tests (H102-H105) are all unsupported: point estimates are small, intervals cross zero, and none provides a meaningful signed interaction above the 0.1 benchmark (H102 +0.041 CI -0.021 to +0.103; H103 +0.002 CI -0.041 to +0.045; H104 -0.038 CI -0.079 to +0.004; H105 -0.067 CI -0.176 to +0.042). I reject them and close further work on those specific modification claims. H106 and H107 show that the MSI-high/WRN association remains very large in screen_batch_a (R116: +0.824; CI +0.766 to +0.882; exposed n=37) and in lower-Cas9 lines (R117: +0.818; CI +0.771 to +0.864; exposed n=50); both have signed lower bounds far above 0.1, so I accept them as dataset-specific robustness checks. I request validation of H92 because H84 attenuated on independent validation and H92 is the accepted low-MYC-expression TP53-loss/USP7 simple effect. Validation of H92 is the most informative way to test whether the broad TP53/USP7 association remains clinically meaningful outside high-MYC contexts. All conclusions remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal effects or claims of external generalizability.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claim and negative values oppose it. For these continuous dependency scores, I continue to use an approximate absolute score-difference benchmark of 0.1 as the practical stand-in for the stated 10% clinical-significance scale, because relative differences are awkward when dependency scores are centered near zero. H51 now has a validation response. Its discovery effect was +0.288 with 95% CI +0.232 to +0.343, and independent validation is +0.264 with an independent interval +0.169 to +0.358. Both cells are adequate, the validation interval excludes zero, and the validation lower bound is above 0.1. I therefore keep H51 accepted and close it: PTEN loss remains associated with more-negative STAT3 dependency specifically within Avana-library lines in this dataset. H92 also has new validation evidence. Its discovery effect was +0.354 with 95% CI +0.221 to +0.487, and independent validation is +0.432 with an independent interval +0.249 to +0.615. Both intervals are compatible with a clinically meaningful less-negative USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines in low-MYC-expression lines, and validation lower bounds are well above the 0.1 benchmark. I keep H92 accepted and close it. This is important because the small MYC-amplified context claim H84 remains unresolved after attenuation: H92 shows that the broader TP53-loss/USP7 association is not confined to high-MYC contexts. Together with accepted non-MYC-amplified H90, high-MYC-expression H91, KRAS-mutant H101, and broadly validated H24, the USP7 conclusion is now supported as a broad dataset association rather than a MYC-restricted context effect. Direct interaction tests H27, H89, and H93, and unresolved small-stratum H84, do not justify restricting the association by KRAS or MYC context. The overall dataset-specific supported associations are therefore: SMARCA4 loss with much more-negative SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much more-negative WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with much less-negative NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss with more-negative STAT3 dependency, including validated Avana-library context; and TP53 loss with less-negative USP7 dependency across broad and important molecular contexts. Negative or unsupported findings include major oncogene-dependency main effects for KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2 in this dataset, broad TP53-loss effects on MDM2/RPL11/POLR2A, MYC-amplification main effects on USP7/DHX9/KIF18A/POLR2A/MDM2, and most tested effect modifications including library, lineage, aneuploidy, PIK3CA, KRAS, MYC-expression, hypoxia, STK11, and interferon-gamma contexts. Remaining uncertainty is mainly about assay-context boundaries: PTEN/STAT3 in non-Avana library lines remains unresolved because non-Avana exposed cells are small, and the exact magnitude of the MYC-amplified USP7/TP53 simple effect remains uncertain. The most informative next analyses are the newly registered low screen-quality robustness checks for USP7/TP53, STAT3/PTEN, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, and NFE2L2/KEAP1. Persistence would make the accepted associations more robust to lower-quality screens; attenuation would define an important assay-context boundary within this dataset. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects or claims of external generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

record.narrative: No evidence assessment is due at this stage. I register new follow-up comparisons that test whether the strongest accepted dataset associations are stable across assay/library contexts rather than being driven mainly by the dominant Avana library, very high screen quality, or high Cas9 activity. The four previously registered low screen_roc_auc checks remain important and should be included in the next analysis batch together with these new claims. I continue to use an approximate absolute dependency-score difference of 0.1 as the practical stand-in for the stated 10% clinical-significance scale, because dependency scores are continuous and often centered near zero, making relative comparisons awkward. For direction -1 claims, the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, meaning exposed lines have stronger/more negative dependency; after signing, a positive estimate supports the claimed direction. For direction +1 claims, the expected raw contrast is positive, meaning exposed lines have weaker/less negative dependency. The new simple-effect claims are deliberately narrow and falsifiable: SMARCA4 loss should show more-negative SMARCA2 dependency in non-Avana library lines if the broad SMARCA4-loss association is not an Avana artifact; KEAP1 loss should show less-negative NFE2L2 dependency in non-Avana library lines; TP53 loss should show less-negative USP7 dependency in non-Avana library lines; and PTEN loss should show more-negative STAT3 dependency specifically within Ky-library lines because the broader non-Avana PTEN comparison has very few exposed observations. I also test low Cas9 activity (<=75%) for all four major axes: SMARCA2/SMARCA4, NFE2L2/KEAP1, USP7/TP53, and STAT3/PTEN. These complement the active low screen_roc_auc checks and the accepted WRN high/low Cas9 and screen-batch robustness checks. If these context-specific estimates remain large and have intervals compatible with the 0.1 benchmark, the dataset conclusions become more robust to library and Cas9-activity heterogeneity. If estimates attenuate or cross zero, we would have a clear assay-context boundary even while accepting the broader average association. All proposals remain comparisons within the supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as causal effects or external generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the proposed association. I used the same practical absolute dependency-score-difference benchmark of about 0.1 for continuous CRISPR dependency scores, together with adequate cell counts and an interval that excludes zero. Nine of the twelve context checks show robust dataset-specific persistence. Low screen_roc_auc (<=0.94) does not attenuate the main associations: TP53 loss remains associated with less-negative USP7 (H110, R121: +0.365; 95% CI +0.229 to +0.501; n=123/535); PTEN loss remains associated with more-negative STAT3 (H111, R122: +0.306; CI +0.211 to +0.402; n=95/563); SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much more-negative SMARCA2 (H112, R123: +0.778; CI +0.741 to +0.814; n=131/527); and KEAP1 loss remains associated with much less-negative NFE2L2 (H113, R124: +0.805; CI +0.770 to +0.840; n=128/530). I accept all four and close them as robustness checks within this dataset. Non-Avana library contexts also persist for SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 (H114, R125: +0.801; CI +0.748 to +0.853; n=61/174) and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 (H115, R126: +0.794; CI +0.746 to +0.842; n=40/195), despite smaller strata. Low Cas9 activity (<=75%) also preserves all four axes: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 (H118, R129: +0.776; CI +0.742 to +0.810; n=137/515), KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 (H119, R130: +0.795; CI +0.758 to +0.832; n=131/521), TP53 loss on USP7 (H120, R131: +0.411; CI +0.291 to +0.531; n=139/513), and PTEN loss on STAT3 (H121, R132: +0.345; CI +0.254 to +0.436; n=100/552). I accept these and close them. The two unresolved boundary cases are USP7/TP53 in non-Avana library (H116, R127: +0.321; CI +0.085 to +0.557; n=43/192) and STAT3/PTEN in Ky-library lines (H117, R128: +0.158; CI +0.063 to +0.254; n=64/399). Both point estimates support the broad accepted directions and exclude zero, but their lower bounds are below the 0.1 practical benchmark, so the evidence does not confirm scientifically meaningful context-specific differences with the same precision. I mark them unresolved. I request validation of H117 because the PTEN/STAT3 association is outside Avana-library remains the most informative remaining context boundary, and validation of this adequately populated Ky-library claim may resolve whether the association retains a practical magnitude outside the dominant library. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal effects or claims of external generalizability.

I continue to use approximately 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference as the practical stand-in for the stated clinical-significance scale, while also considering interval precision, cell counts, and independent validation. The validation interval excludes zero and its lower bound is above the 0.1 practical benchmark. H84, the TP53-loss effect on USP7 specifically among MYC-amplified lines, remains uncertain in magnitude: discovery was large (R90: +0.510; 95% CI +0.345 to +0.674), and independent validation remained positive and just excluded zero (R106: +0.266; independent interval +0.012 to +0.521), but the validation lower bound is below the 0.1 practical benchmark. I keep H84 unresolved and closed as a small-stratum context estimate. This does not weaken the broad validated TP53-loss/less-negative USP7 association (H24), which is also supported by accepted contexts H90, H91, H92, H101, H110, H114/H120 and others. H27, the interaction testing whether TP53 loss modifies USP7 dependency specifically in KRAS-mutant lines relative to KRAS-wild-type lines, remains unsupported: discovery was near zero (R28: +0.018; CI -0.152 to +0.188) and independent validation was negative with an interval crossing zero (R107: -0.101; independent interval -0.347 to +0.144). record.narrative:
No evidence assessment is due at this stage. I keep the four pending Ky-library robustness checks (H122-H125) in the active queue and register a focused follow-up set that addresses the next major biological question after library/Cas9/screen-quality robustness: whether MYC expression alters the magnitude of the accepted dataset-specific associations. I use high versus low rnaseq_MYC_log2_tpm (threshold 5.0) as a biologically motivated context assay, not as a causal biomarker. For each accepted main axis, I test an interaction signed toward the accepted main effect: high MYC expression would strengthen more-negative WRN dependency in MSI-high lines, more-negative SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines, more-negative STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss lines, less-negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines, and less-negative USP7 dependency in TP53-loss lines. These adequately populated context tests can either extend the accepted conclusions across a transcriptional/growth-stress phenotype or define a MYC-expression boundary.

I also register two mechanistically motivated refinements for the two most coherent axes. First, if SWI/SNF co-loss deepens SMARCA2 dependency, ARID1A loss within SMARCA4-loss lines should be associated with more-negative SMARCA2 scores, even though broad ARID1A loss was null. Second, because USP7 and p53 pathway biology may vary with p16/CDKN2A status, I test TP53-loss-associated less-negative USP7 dependency specifically among CDKN2A-loss lines; H98 gave adequate cells in this co-loss subgroup. Finally, I add a broad new untested predictor/outcome pair: MYC amplification versus STAT3 dependency. This is a falsifiable screen for whether MYC-amplified lines have stronger STAT3 dependency. All proposals remain within this supplied dataset and use the same practical absolute dependency-score benchmark of about 0.1.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
