Iteration 11/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The main accepted dataset-specific associations remain unchanged, and the previously registered Ky-library robustness checks (H122-H125), MYC-expression interaction checks (H126-H129), and co-loss/new-predictor checks (H131-H133) remain active pending evidence. Missing evidence for those claims is not treated as null evidence.

For this exploration, I add two classes of comparisons. First, I extend robustness testing for the four accepted axes that are not yet complete under high Cas9 editing activity, high screen ROC-AUC, and batch A. High Cas9 activity is a useful boundary because strong association in low-Cas9 strata (H118-H121) could raise a question of editing-efficiency dependence; if these associations also hold when cas9_activity_pct is at least 80%, that supports robustness against Cas9-activity variation. High screen ROC-AUC complements the accepted low-ROC contexts and helps determine whether the effects are confined to poorer screens. Batch A testing is useful because only WRN/MSI-high has been checked in batch A so far; if SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, TP53-loss/USP7, and PTEN-loss/STAT3 also hold in batch A, batch-specific artifacts become less likely. Expected directions are the same accepted dataset-specific directions: SMARCA4 loss raw lower/more negative SMARCA2; KEAP1 loss raw higher/less negative NFE2L2; TP53 loss raw higher/less negative USP7; PTEN loss raw lower/more negative STAT3.

Second, I register two mechanistic new predictor/outcome screens. MYC amplification versus dependency_WRN is falsifiable but plausible: MYC-driven replication/transcription stress could strengthen WRN helicase dependency, yielding a more-negative dependency score in MYC-amplified lines. RB1 loss versus dependency_DHX9 is also plausible but not strong prior: E2F-driven transcriptional and replication stress from RB1 loss could alter dependency on DHX9-associated transcription/replication stress responses. If either shows an adequately sized signed effect, it would be a new dataset-specific association; if null, it simply narrows the space of plausible predictor-outcome relationships. I continue to use an approximately 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference as the practical scientific benchmark for these signed continuous CRISPR dependency scores, because the task's 10% relative-change threshold is not well-defined for signed dependency scores and interval width near zero matters strongly. All proposals remain associations within this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims. Validation capacity is zero, so the main value of these proposals is discovery and context-boundary refinement.

Iteration 12/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction, so a positive signed value supports the hypothesis and a negative signed value opposes it. For dependency scores, I use an approximate 0.1 absolute signed difference as the practical benchmark for scientific meaningfulness because relative-change thresholds are unstable for signed scores. H122, H123, and H124 show very large positive signed effects in the CRISPR library Ky context: MSI-high versus WRN, SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2, and KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2. The confidence intervals are entirely far above the 0.1 benchmark, and cell counts are adequate despite smaller strata. I therefore accept these as dataset-specific robustness checks showing that these associations are not confined to the Avana library. H125 tests TP53 loss versus USP7 in the Ky library. The point estimate is positive and above the practical benchmark, +0.212, but the 95% interval reaches down to +0.051, so the evidence does not confidently place the context-specific effect above the 0.1 benchmark. I therefore leave it unresolved and closed because validation capacity is exhausted. H134 through H137 test high Cas9 activity boundaries for the main axes. All have positive signed effects with intervals excluding zero and lower bounds above the practical benchmark, so they support robustness of the main associations when Cas9 activity is high. H138 and H139 complete high screen ROC-AUC contexts for KEAP1/NFE2L2 and TP53/USP7; both are positive, large-to-moderate, and confident, so they are accepted. H144 and H145 are new broad predictor screens. Their intervals are statistically separated from zero but the signed estimates are negative relative to the claimed direction and small: about -0.033 and -0.035, with upper bounds below 0.065. These are not meaningful associations in the proposed direction and are better interpreted as very small opposite effects or multiple-testing noise than as evidence of biologically meaningful dependency changes. I reject them as meaningful claims. I also close the previously deferred unresolved items H40 and H52 because there is no remaining validation capacity and no new evidence can escalate them; this is not evidence of absence. Overall, the strongest dataset-specific associations remain robust across library, Cas9-activity, and screen-quality contexts, while new small predictor effects are not supported at a practical magnitude. These remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Response deadline: H117 tests whether PTEN loss is associated with a more-negative dependency_STAT3 score in CRISPR-library Ky samples. The estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so a positive estimate supports the hypothesis. Discovery R128 was +0.158 (95% CI +0.063 to +0.254; n=64/399), and independent validation R133 was +0.346 (independent interval +0.177 to +0.514; n=67/466). The validation interval excludes zero and its lower bound is above the practical dependency-score benchmark of about 0.1 absolute units. I therefore accept H117 and keep it closed. This is a dataset-specific robustness/context result: PTEN loss remains associated with stronger, i.e. more-negative, STAT3 dependency in the Ky-library stratum. It complements the validated Avana result H51 (R55, R93) and the overall validated effect H11 (R11, R40). It does not by itself establish causality or external generalizability.

Final scientific report at this point. Main accepted dataset-specific associations. 1) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much more-negative dependency_SMARCA2. The main effect is H6/R6 +0.784, validated by R66 +0.780. Robust context checks include low and high screen_roc_auc, low and high Cas9 activity, multiple libraries including Ky H123/R135, and non-Avana strata H114/R125. The practical magnitude is large and stable. 2) MSI-high is associated with much more-negative dependency_WRN. The main effect is H7/R7 +0.790, validated by R39 +0.822. Robust contexts include adherent culture H50/R54, high Cas9 H77/R83, high ROC H78/R84, low ROC H97/R102, low Cas9 H107/R117, batch A H106/R116, and Ky library H122/R134. The effect is very large and repeatedly detected. 3) KEAP1 loss is associated with much less-negative dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted signed effect is H17/R5 +0.796, validated by R79 +0.792. Context checks across low/high Cas9, low/high ROC, TP53-loss status, lineage subtype, low/high MYC expression subgroups, and Ky/non-Avana library contexts are largely consistent, for example H75/R82, H80/R86, H94/R99, H113/R124, H115/R126, H119/R130, H124/R136, H135/R139, H138/R142. 4) PTEN loss is associated with more-negative dependency_STAT3. The main effect is H11/R11 +0.267, validated by R40 +0.309. It is robust in Avana H51/R55/R93, high Cas9 H137/R141, low Cas9 H121/R132, high ROC H82/R88, low ROC H111/R122, and now Ky H117/R128/R133. 5) TP53 loss is associated with less-negative dependency_USP7, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. The main effect is H24/R24 +0.396, validated by R26 +0.437. It is robust in several contexts, including low and high MYC expression H92/R97/R120 and H91/R96, high and low Cas9 H136/R140 and H120/R131, and high/low ROC H139/R143 and H110/R121. However, some library or small-stratum contexts remain only uncertain in magnitude, not clearly absent.

Negative findings. The supplied data do not support scientifically meaningful dependency-score differences for most tested single driver copy-number or mutation predictors. Examples: KRAS mutation versus dependency_KRAS H1/R1; BRAF V600E versus dependency_BRAF H2/R2; EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR H3/R3/R13 and versus TMED10/RIT1 in tested strata H16/R17 and H109/R119; ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 in broad and tested strata H4/R4, H71/R76, H87/R110, H100/R105; TP53 loss versus dependency_MDM2 H8/R8; MYC amplification versus USP7 H9/R9, DHX9 H10/R10, KIF18A H15/R16, POLR2A H53/R57, and WRN H144/R144; RB1 loss versus DHX9 H145/R145; PIK3CA, STK11, SMAD4, NF1, RB1, BRCA2, ARID1A broad effects, and artificial research markers D/E/F are not associated with meaningful dependency differences. Many of these intervals exclude large practical effects or are centered near zero. Some tiny signed effects reached statistical separation but were below the practical benchmark and should not be interpreted as meaningful dependencies.

Interaction findings are mostly negative. The data do not support meaningful modification of the accepted main axes by ARID1A loss for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 H28/R29; lineage subtype for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 H59/R63, WRN/MSI-high H30/R31, or KEAP1/NFE2L2 H60/R64; culture type for WRN/MSI-high after validation H42/R45/R53; aneuploidy for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 H104/R114, STAT3/PTEN H105/R115, WRN/MSI-high H102/R112, or KEAP1/NFE2L2 H103/R113; hypoxia, STK11, IFN-gamma, or tested co-losses for NFE2L2/KEAP1 or WRN/MSI-high; KRAS context for USP7/TP53 after validation H27/R28/R107; and MYC-expression interaction for USP7/TP53 H93/R98/H130/R98. These negative interaction results do not prove absence of all interactions, but they argue against many proposed subgroup-conditioned effects in this dataset.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main associations are well supported, but some context-specific magnitudes are not confidently above the practical benchmark because of wide intervals or small strata and no remaining validation capacity. H40/R43 and H52/R56 leave non-Avana STAT3/PTEN uncertain overall and in the non-Avana simple effect. H116/R127 and H125/R137 leave TP53-loss/USP7 uncertain in non-Avana and Ky contexts, with positive point estimates but lower bounds below the practical benchmark. H84/R90/R106 leaves TP53-loss/USP7 in MYC-amplified lines uncertain because validation lower bound was only +0.012. H72/R77 was invalid because of insufficient cell counts, so no conclusion can be drawn from it. Active but untested claims H126-H129 MYC-expression interactions, H131-H132 co-loss refinements, H133 MYC amplification versus STAT3, and H140-H143 batch A checks are not null; missing evidence is not evidence of absence.

Most informative next analyses. With zero remaining validation capacity, the best next step is to complete already registered discovery boundary checks. The highest-priority active queue is batch A simple effects for the main accepted axes: H140 SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, H141 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, H142 TP53-loss/USP7, and H143 PTEN-loss/STAT3. Only WRN/MSI-high has been directly checked in batch A so far H106/R116, so these would test whether batch A is a technical confounder for the four other main associations. I also registered a final library-context simple effect, MSI-high/dependency_WRN within Avana as a refinement of H7, to complete the library-boundary set for the main axes. If further slots are available, the MYC-expression interaction checks H126-H129 and the co-loss refinements H131-H132/H133 are scientifically useful but less urgent for the central claims.

All conclusions are dataset-specific associations in this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dependency dataset. They do not establish that the measured predictors cause the dependency-score differences, and they do not establish external generalizability to other cell lines, tissues, or experimental systems. For the signed CRISPR dependency scores, I used an approximate 0.1 absolute-score practical benchmark alongside the supplied 10% relative-significance rule because relative changes are unstable for signed scores crossing near zero.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

No assessments are due because no new evidence has arrived since the last synthesis. The accepted dataset-specific main axes remain unchanged, and I continue to interpret them as associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not as causal or externally generalizable claims. The highest-priority active queue still contains robustness and boundary checks, but I register additional comparisons that target scientifically distinct questions.

First, I add new predictor-outcome screens with explicit mechanistic hypotheses. MTAP loss is proposed as a candidate modifier of WRN dependency because MTAP deletion alters methionine salvage and one-carbon/replication-stress biology; WRN is a helicase relevant to replication stress, so I anticipate a more negative dependency_WRN score in MTAP-loss lines, a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast. TP53 loss is tested against STAT3 dependency as a new cross-pathway hypothesis: p53 loss may remodel stress signaling and STAT3 activity, and I frame the hypothesis as weaker STAT3 dependency under p53 loss, i.e. a raw less-negative/positive contrast. CDKN2A loss is tested against MDM2 dependency because loss of p14ARF could reduce cellular reliance on MDM2-p53 homeostasis, predicting less-negative dependency_MDM2. PTEN loss in KRAS-wildtype lines is tested because PI3K pathway activation can bypass upstream KRAS signaling; the hypothesis is that KRAS dependency becomes weaker, a raw positive contrast. STK11 loss is similarly tested against KRAS dependency because LKB1 loss can alter downstream metabolic and growth signaling, potentially weakening KRAS dependence. EGFR amplification is tested against ERBB2 dependency because receptor tyrosine kinase redundancy may reduce dependence on one paralogous kinase; the hypothesis is weaker ERBB2 dependency, though co-amplification or compensatory signaling are plausible alternatives.

Second, I add refinement checks for accepted associations where context-specific magnitude remains uncertain or a technical boundary is unresolved. The KEAP1 loss/dependency_NFE2L2 association is well supported overall and in several quality and library contexts, but culture condition is a plausible biological boundary. The registered interaction tests whether the KEAP1 effect is weaker in adherent culture than in the nonadherent complement. I specify this as a negative raw interaction in adherent culture; the opposite would suggest nonadherent culture attenuates rather than amplifies the effect. For the unresolved Ky-library TP53-loss/dependency_USP7 result, I test the association in Ky-library samples with high screen quality, screen_roc_auc at least 0.95, to determine whether the Ky uncertainty is driven by lower-quality screens. For the unresolved MYC-amplified TP53-loss/dependency_USP7 result, I similarly test the MYC-amplified stratum restricted to high screen quality, which may clarify whether the small validation lower bound reflects poor screen quality rather than absence of the association.

I continue to use approximately 0.1 absolute signed dependency-score difference as a practical scientific benchmark, alongside the supplied 10% relative-change guidance, because dependency scores are signed and relative changes are unstable near zero. With zero remaining validation capacity, these proposals are discovery and context-boundary analyses only. Missing evidence is not evidence of absence.

prompt:
Iteration 13/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The highest-priority active queue still contains robustness and boundary checks, but I register additional comparisons that target scientifically distinct questions.\n\nFirst, I add new predictor-outcome screens with explicit mechanistic hypotheses. MTAP loss is proposed as a candidate modifier of WRN dependency because MTAP deletion alters methionine salvage and one-carbon/replication-stress biology; WRN is a helicase relevant to replication stress, so I anticipate a more negative dependency_WRN score in MTAP-loss lines, a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast. CDKN2A loss is tested against MDM2 dependency because loss of p14ARF could reduce cellular reliance on MDM2-p53 homeostasis, predicting less-negative dependency_MDM2. PTEN loss in KRAS-wildtype lines is tested because PI3K pathway activation can bypass upstream KRAS signaling; the hypothesis is that KRAS dependency becomes weaker, a raw positive contrast. STK11 loss is similarly tested against KRAS dependency because LKB1 loss can alter downstream metabolic and growth signaling, potentially weakening KRAS dependence. EGFR amplification is tested against ERBB2 dependency because receptor tyrosine kinase redundancy may reduce dependence on one paralogous kinase; the hypothesis is weaker ERBB2 dependency, though co-amplification or compensatory signaling are plausible alternatives.\n\nSecond, I add refinement checks for accepted associations where context-specific magnitude remains uncertain or a technical boundary is unresolved. The KEAP1 loss/dependency_NFE2L2 association is well supported overall and in several quality and library contexts, but culture condition is a plausible biological boundary. record.narrative: No assessments are due because no new evidence has arrived since the last synthesis, so this analyze step only allocates analysis slots. I selected 12 already registered, still-active, untested comparisons. The priority is to strengthen and resolve the already accepted dataset-specific main axes before adding broad speculative screens. Positive signed estimates for these registered hypotheses would support the registered association direction; negative estimates would not support it. If any comparison is invalid for insufficient cell size, it gives no evidence either way. No validation requests are made because no validation capacity remains. All interpretations remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All returned estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction, so positive signed estimates support the registered hypothesis and negative signed estimates oppose it. For signed CRISPR dependency scores, I continued to use an approximate 0.1 absolute signed-score difference as a practical benchmark for scientific meaningfulness, because relative changes are unstable when scores are centered near zero; the supplied 10% relative threshold is also noted, but the absolute benchmark is more interpretable here.
